en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: 'informed us', while the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) never ate his fill of wheat bread for three consecutive days until he passed away.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: 'informed us', and Zuhayr said: 'narrated to us'—Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: 'The family of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) never ate their fill of wheat food for three consecutive nights from the time he arrived in Medina until he was taken.'

Abu Bakr ibn an-Nadr ibn Abi an-Nadr narrated to us: Abu an-Nadr, Hashim ibn al-Qasim, narrated to me: 'Ubaydullah al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan ath-Thawri, from 'Ubayd al-Muktib, from Fudayl, from ash-Sha'bi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when he laughed and said, 'Do you know what I am laughing at?' He said: We said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'At the servant's dialogue with his Lord. He says, "O my Lord, did You not grant me protection against injustice?" He said: He says, "Yes indeed." He said: So he says, "Then I do not permit any witness against myself except a witness from me." He said: So He says, "Sufficient is yourself today as a witness against you, and the noble scribes as witnesses." He said: Then a seal is placed over his mouth and it is said to his limbs, "Speak." He said: So they speak of his deeds. He said: Then he is allowed to speak again. He said: So he says, "Away with you, and ruin unto you! It was on your behalf that I was contending!"'

Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?' He said, 'Do you harm one another in seeing the sun at midday when there is no cloud?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'Do you harm one another in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will not harm one another in seeing your Lord except as you harm one another in seeing one of the two.' He said: 'Then He meets the servant and says, "O so-and-so, did I not honor you, make you a leader, marry you, subject horses and camels to you, and leave you to lead and take a fourth of the spoils?" He will say, "Yes indeed." He said: Then He will say, "Did you think that you would meet Me?" He will say, "No." So He will say, "Then I forget you just as you forgot Me." Then He meets the second and says, "O so-and-so, did I not honor you, make you a leader, marry you, subject horses and camels to you, and leave you to lead and take a fourth of the spoils?" He will say, "Yes indeed, O my Lord." He will say, "Did you think that you would meet Me?" He will say, "No." So He will say, "Then I forget you just as you forgot Me." Then He meets the third and says the like of that to him, so he says, "O my Lord, I believed in You, in Your Book, and in Your messengers, and I prayed, fasted, and gave charity," and he praises with good as much as he can. So He says, "Right here, then." He said: Then it is said to him, "Now We send Our witness against you." And he wonders to himself, "Who is it that could testify against me?" Then a seal is placed over his mouth, and it is said to his thigh, his flesh, and his bones, "Speak." So his thigh, his flesh, and his bones speak of his deeds. And that is so he cannot excuse himself. And that is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom Allah is displeased.'

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Khalid ibn 'Umayr, who said: I heard 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan saying: 'I saw myself as the seventh of seven with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), having no food except the leaves of the hublah tree until the corners of our mouths became ulcerated.'

Ishaq ibn 'Umar ibn Salit narrated to me: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Khalid ibn 'Umayr—and he had reached the pre-Islamic period of ignorance—who said: 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan, who was the governor over Basra, delivered a sermon... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Shayban.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Khalid ibn 'Umayr al-'Adawi, who said: 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan delivered a sermon to us; he praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said: 'To proceed: Indeed, this world has announced its severance and has turned away swiftly, and nothing remains of it except a remnant like the remnant of water left in a vessel that its owner drains. And you are moving from it to an abode that has no end, so depart with the best of what is with you. For indeed, it was mentioned to us that a stone is thrown from the edge of Hellfire and plunges into it for 70 years without reaching its bottom, and by Allah, it will surely be filled—are you amazed? And it was mentioned to us that between two side-posts of the gates of Paradise is the distance of 40 years' travel, and there will surely come a day upon it when it will be crowded with people. And I saw myself as the seventh of seven with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), having no food except tree leaves until the corners of our mouths became ulcerated. Then I found a cloak and tore it in half between myself and Sa'd ibn Malik; I wore half of it as a waist-wrapper and Sa'd wore half of it as a waist-wrapper. Yet today there is none of us except that he has become a governor over one of the major cities. And indeed, I seek refuge with Allah from being great in my own eyes while being small in the sight of Allah. And never was there a prophethood except that it gradually changed until its final outcome became kingship, so you will soon come to know and experience the rulers after us.'

And Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Waki' informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with this chain of narration, and he said: '...until one of us would pass stool just as a goat does, mixing nothing with it.'

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Isma'il, from Qays, from Sa'd [H]; and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father and Ibn Bishr narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Qays, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas saying: 'By Allah, I am indeed the first man among the Arabs to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah. And we used to go on expeditions with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) having no food to eat except the leaves of the hublah and this samur tree, until one of us would pass stool just as a sheep does. Then the Banu Asad came to censure me regarding religion; I would surely then be ruined and my deed gone astray!' And Ibn Numayr did not say 'then'.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's; 'Abbas said: 'narrated to us', and Ishaq said: 'informed us'—Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us: Bukayr ibn Mismar narrated to us: 'Amir ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was among his camels when his son 'Umar came to him. When Sa'd saw him, he said, 'I seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this rider.' So he dismounted and said to him, 'Have you settled among your camels and your sheep and left the people contending for kingship among themselves?' Sa'd struck him on his chest and said, 'Be silent! I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, Allah loves the servant who is pious, self-sufficient, and hidden."'

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'There were three men among the Children of Israel: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. Allah willed to test them, so He sent an angel to them. He came to the leper and said, "What thing is most beloved to you?" He said, "A fair complexion, beautiful skin, and that what makes people loathe me be removed from me." He said: So he wiped him, and his loathsomeness was removed from him, and he was given a fair complexion and beautiful skin. He said, "Then what wealth is most beloved to you?" He said, "Camels"—or he said "cattle", Ishaq was in doubt, except that either the leper or the bald man said camels and the other said cattle. He said: So he was given a pregnant she-camel, and he said, "May Allah bless you in it." He said: Then he came to the bald man and said, "What thing is most beloved to you?" He said, "Beautiful hair, and that this which makes people loathe me be removed from me." He said: So he wiped him, and it departed from him, and he was given beautiful hair. He said, "Then what wealth is most beloved to you?" He said, "Cattle." So he was given a pregnant cow, and he said, "May Allah bless you in it." He said: Then he came to the blind man and said, "What thing is most beloved to you?" He said, "That Allah restores my sight to me so that I may see the people with it." He said: So he wiped him, and Allah restored his sight to him. He said, "Then what wealth is most beloved to you?" He said, "Sheep." So he was given a female sheep with lambs. Then both of these [animals] reproduced and this one gave birth, so that this one had a valley of camels, that one had a valley of cattle, and this one had a valley of sheep. He said: Then he came to the leper in his former appearance and form, and said, "A poor man, whose means have been cut off in my journey, so I have no means of reaching my destination today except by Allah and then by you. I ask you by the One Who gave you the fair complexion, the beautiful skin, and the wealth, for a camel with which I may reach my destination on my journey." But he said, "The rights [obligations] are many." So he said to him, "It is as if I know you; were you not a leper whom people loathed, a poor man, and Allah gave you?" He said, "I only inherited this wealth from ancestor after ancestor." So he said, "If you are lying, may Allah restore you to what you were." He said: And he came to the bald man in his former appearance and said to him the like of what he said to this one, and he replied to him with the like of what this one replied. So he said, "If you are lying, may Allah restore you to what you were." He said: And he came to the blind man in his former appearance and form and said, "A poor man and a wayfarer whose means have been cut off in my journey, so I have no means of reaching my destination today except by Allah and then by you. I ask you by the One Who restored your sight to you for a sheep with which I may reach my destination on my journey." He said, "I was indeed blind and Allah restored my sight to me, so take what you wish and leave what you wish, for by Allah, I will not burden you today with anything you take for Allah's sake." So he said, "Keep your wealth, for you have only been tested; indeed, Allah is pleased with you and displeased with your two companions."'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us [H]; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us [H]; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Look at those who are lower than you and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the blessing of Allah.' Abu Mu'awiyah said: 'upon you.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), exactly the like of the hadith of Abu az-Zinad.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—Qutaybah said: 'narrated to us', and Yahya said: 'informed us'—al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Hizami, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'When one of you looks at someone who has been favored over him in wealth and physical form, let him look at someone who is lower than him, over whom he has been favored.'

'Amr ibn Sawwad al-'Amiri narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him that Yazid ibn Rabah—he is Abu Firas, the freed slave of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As—narrated to him, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that he said: 'When Persia and Rome are conquered for you, what kind of people will you be?' 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Awf said: 'We will say what Allah commanded us.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Or other than that: you will compete with one another, then envy one another, then turn your backs on one another, then hate one another—or something to that effect—then you will turn to the poor among the Muhajirun and set some of them against the necks of others.'

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih [H]; and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, both from az-Zuhri, with the chain of Yunus and the like of his hadith, except that in the hadith of Salih it is: 'and distract you just as it distracted them.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya ibn 'Abdullah—meaning Ibn Harmalah ibn 'Imran at-Tujibi—narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn az-Zubayr, that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him that 'Amr ibn 'Awf—and he was an ally of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy and had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah to Bahrain to collect its jizyah, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had made peace with the people of Bahrain and appointed al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami over them. Abu 'Ubaydah arrived with wealth from Bahrain, and the Ansar heard of Abu 'Ubaydah's arrival, so they attended the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished praying, he turned around and they presented themselves to him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) smiled when he saw them, then said: 'I think you have heard that Abu 'Ubaydah has arrived with something from Bahrain?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Then rejoice and hope for what will please you! For by Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear for you that worldly wealth will be spread out before you just as it was spread out before those who came before you, so you will compete for it just as they competed for it, and it will destroy you just as it destroyed them.'

Yahya ibn Yahya at-Tamimi and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, both from Ibn 'Uyaynah—Yahya said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us—from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Three follow the deceased, then two return and one remains: his family, his wealth, and his deeds follow him; then his family and his wealth return, and his deeds remain.'
And Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated it to me: Ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: Al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman informed me, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The servant says: "My wealth! My wealth!" Yet he only possesses three things of his wealth: what he eats and exhausts, or wears out and ruins, or gives and stores up. And whatever is besides that will pass away, and he leaves it for the people.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; and they both said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id [H]; and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to us, all of them from Qatadah, from Mutarrif, from his father, who said: I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Hammam.

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from his father, who said: I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was reciting: {Competition in worldly increase diverts you}. He said: 'The son of Adam says: "My wealth! My wealth!" He said: And do you have, O son of Adam, anything of your wealth except what you ate and exhausted, or wore and wore out, or gave in charity and enacted?'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah as-Sami narrated to me, both saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning ath-Thaqafi—narrated to us, from Ja'far, from his father, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that in the hadith of ath-Thaqafi it is: 'Even if it were alive, this shortness of ears would be a defect in it.'

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Ja'far, from his father, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed through the marketplace, entering from one of the elevated areas while people were on both sides of him. He passed by a dead young kid with tiny ears, took hold of it by its ear, and then said: 'Which of you would like to have this for a dirham?' They said: 'We would not like to have it for anything; what would we do with it?' He said: 'Would you like to have it for free?' They said: 'By Allah, even if it were alive, it would be defective because it has tiny ears, so how now when it is dead?' He said: 'By Allah, the world is more insignificant to Allah than this is to you.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning ad-Darawardi—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he mentioned a number of hadiths among which was that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, in man there is a bone that the earth never consumes; upon it he will be reconstructed on the Day of Resurrection.' They said: 'Which bone is it, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The coccyx.'

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'All of the son of Adam will be consumed by the earth except the coccyx; from it he was created and upon it he will be reconstructed.'

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Between the two blowings is forty.' They said: 'O Abu Hurayrah, forty days?' He said: 'I decline.' They said: 'Forty months?' He said: 'I decline.' They said: 'Forty years?' He said: 'I decline. Then Allah sends down water from the sky, and they will sprout just as herbs sprout.' He said: 'And there is nothing of a human being that does not decay except one bone, which is the coccyx, and from it creation will be reconstructed on the Day of Resurrection.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The Hour will be established while a man is milking a milch-camel, and the vessel will not even reach his mouth before it is established; and two men will be trading a garment, and they will not even complete its trade before it is established; and a man will be plastering his watering basin, and he will not even leave it before it is established.'

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, who said: A boy belonging to al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah passed by—and he was of my age group—so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'If this [boy] lives on, old age will not overtake him before the Hour is established.'
